belief_records.strategy: Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk of exploitation; update beliefs from encounter behavior and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate when expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk of helping a selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed play and choose actions to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate when expected gains to good players outweigh the benefit of exploiting a potentially selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; use encounter evidence to update beliefs and defect against likely selfish players.
Defect each round: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; D strictly dominates C.
Cooperate when expected to improve total good-player welfare; use encounter outcomes and messages as evidence, while accounting for selfish players’ incentives.
Cooperate when a good opponent is likely to reciprocate; use encounter behavior to update beliefs and adapt across rounds.
Cooperate when it best supports the good players’ shared welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and use defection when it improves expected welfare against selfish opponents.
As a selfish player, choose the payoff-maximizing action each round; here, D strictly dominates C.
Cooperate with a likely good opponent to maximize good players’ combined payoff; adjust beliefs and actions as encounter evidence accumulates.
Defect when the risk of helping a selfish opponent outweighs the cooperation benefit; update identity beliefs from observed actions and prioritize total payoff of good players.
Cooperate when doing so best supports expected total payoff for good players; use observed actions and claims as uncertain evidence when updating identity beliefs.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; use observed actions to update identity beliefs.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff whatever the opponent chooses. P3’s cooperation indicates they are good; otherwise beliefs follow the conditioned prior.
Defect: in a one-time encounter, D strictly dominates C regardless of P4’s action or promise.
Cooperate when it best supports expected welfare among good players; treat promises as weak evidence and update from observed actions.

Cooperate when it best supports good players’ shared welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and use defection when it improves expected welfare against selfish opponents.

Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation in this one-time encounter. P4 and P7 cooperated against my defection, so I infer they are good; distribute remaining uncertainty across the other players.
Cooperate with P8: if they’re good, mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare; if selfish, they may defect. Update identity beliefs from actions, treating promises as weak evidence.

Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good type, but treat claims as unverified. Defect here given the high posterior chance P7 is selfish; adapt future choices to observed actions and beliefs.
